_meta.about: Learning-mode content. Keys match the classifier class names exactly.
sources: Nandikesvara, Abhinaya Darpana, English translation by A. Coomaraswamy and G. K. Duggirala (1917, public domain): finger formations
Wikipedia, List of mudras (dance): English translations and traditional uses
Cross-checked against teaching blogs and articles where finger formations differ between schools
_meta.note: Descriptions are written in our own words. Schools of Bharatanatyam describe a few gestures slightly differently, so entries with a note field should be checked against the dataset photos.

Pathaka.form: Straighten all four fingers and press them together. Fold the thumb in against the base of the index finger.
Pathaka.uses: Beginning a dance, Forest, River, Clouds, Night, Forbidding, Sprinkling Water

Tripathaka.form: Start from Pataka and bend only the ring finger down. The index, middle and little fingers stay straight.
Tripathaka.uses: Tree, Arrow, Crown, Indra, Rising Flame

Ardhapathaka.form: Start from Tripataka and bend the little finger down as well. Only the index and middle fingers stay straight.
Ardhapathaka.uses: tender shoots, riverbank, writing panel, knife, temple tower, horn

Katrimukha.form: Fold the ring and little fingers toward the thumb and open the index and middle fingers apart, like a pair of scissors.
Katrimukha.uses: separation, opposition, stealing, lightning, disagreement, corner of the eye
Katrimukha.note: The old text spreads the index and little fingers instead. Follow the reference photo.

Mayura.form: Touch the tip of the ring finger to the thumb. The index, middle and little fingers stay extended.
Mayura.uses: peacock's beak, bird of omen, stroking the hair, wiping tears, argument

Ardhachandran.form: Hold a Pataka, with the fingers straight and together, and stretch the thumb out to the side.

Aralam.form: Hold a Pataka and curl the index finger inward like a hook. The other fingers stay straight.

Shukatundam.form: Start from Arala and also bend the ring finger. The index finger stays curved, and the middle and little fingers stay extended.
Shukatundam.uses: shooting an arrow, throwing a spear, mystery

Mushti.form: Curl all four fingers into the palm and rest the thumb over them.
Mushti.uses: steadiness, holding things, grasping the hair, wrestling

Sikharam.form: Make a fist and raise the thumb straight up.
Sikharam.uses: God of Love, bow, pillar, silence, questioning, embrace

Kapith.form: Make Shikhara, then curl the index finger over the top of the raised thumb.
Kapith.uses: Lakshmi, Saraswati, holding cymbals, holding flowers, milking cows

Katakamukha_1.form: Bring the tips of the index and middle fingers to the thumb, so the three form an opening like a bracelet clasp. The ring and little fingers rest slightly raised and apart.
Katakamukha_1.uses: picking flowers, holding a garland or pearl necklace, drawing a bow, speech, glancing
Katakamukha_1.note: Katakamukha is shown in three recognised ways. Follow the reference photo for the exact finger positions of this variant.

Katakamukha_2.form: Bring the tips of the index and middle fingers to the thumb, so the three form an opening like a bracelet clasp. The ring and little fingers rest slightly raised and apart.
Katakamukha_2.uses: picking flowers, holding a garland or pearl necklace, drawing a bow, speech, glancing
Katakamukha_2.note: Katakamukha is shown in three recognised ways. Follow the reference photo for the exact finger positions of this variant.

Katakamukha_3.form: Bring the tips of the index and middle fingers to the thumb, so the three form an opening like a bracelet clasp. The ring and little fingers rest slightly raised and apart.
Katakamukha_3.uses: picking flowers, holding a garland or pearl necklace, drawing a bow, speech, glancing
Katakamukha_3.note: Katakamukha is shown in three recognised ways. Follow the reference photo for the exact finger positions of this variant.

Suchi.form: Fold the middle, ring and little fingers against the thumb and point the index finger straight up.
Suchi.uses: the number one, the sun, the world, threatening, astonishment, umbrella, beating a drum

Chandrakala.form: Start from Suchi and release the thumb outward, so the index finger and thumb are extended and the other fingers stay folded.

Padmakosha.form: Spread the fingers and thumb and curve them slightly, with the palm hollowed, as if holding a ball or a lotus bud.
Padmakosha.uses: fruit, wood apple, mango, flower bud, breast, bell shape

Sarpasirsha.form: Keep the fingers straight and together as in Pataka, but hollow the palm so the hand forms a cupped snake's head.
Sarpasirsha.uses: snake, giving water to gods and sages, elephant's ears, slowness

Mrigasirsha.form: Start from the cupped Sarpashirsha hand, with the fingers together, and extend the thumb and little finger outward.
Mrigasirsha.uses: women, calling the beloved, cheek, fear, house, discussion, holding an umbrella
Mrigasirsha.note: Teachers describe this slightly differently. Follow the reference photo.

Simhamukham.form: Touch the tips of the middle and ring fingers to the thumb. The index and little fingers stay extended.
Simhamukham.uses: lion, elephant, pearl, coral, fragrance, a drop of water

Kangulam.form: Spread the thumb, index and middle fingers, bend the ring finger in, and keep the little finger upright.
Kangulam.uses: lakuca fruit, water lily, small bells, anything small

Alapadmam.form: Spread all the fingers wide and curve them back, like a fully opened lotus.
Alapadmam.uses: full-blown lotus, yearning for the beloved, mirror, full moon, village, praise

Chaturam.form: Bend the thumb to touch the base of the ring finger. Keep the index, middle and ring fingers straight and together, with the little finger extended slightly apart.
Chaturam.uses: musk, a little, eyes, playful talk, breaking to pieces
Chaturam.note: Teachers describe this slightly differently. Follow the reference photo.

Bramaram.form: Touch the thumb to the middle finger, fold the index finger in, and keep the ring and little fingers extended.

Hamsasyam.form: Touch the tip of the index finger to the thumb and keep the other three fingers extended and slightly apart.
Hamsasyam.uses: tying the marriage thread, initiation, painting, a drop of water, pearl

Hamsapaksha.form: Start from the cupped Sarpashirsha hand, with the fingers together, and extend the little finger.
Hamsapaksha.uses: building a bridge, making marks with the nails, arranging, the number six
Hamsapaksha.note: Teachers describe this slightly differently. Follow the reference photo.

Mukulam.form: Bring all the fingertips together with the thumb, like a closed bud.
Mukulam.uses: water lily, God of Love, eating, bud

Tamarachudam.form: Bring the fingertips together as in Mukula, then bend the index finger.
Tamarachudam.uses: rooster, crane, camel, calf, writing or drawing
Tamarachudam.note: Teachers describe this slightly differently. Follow the reference photo.

Trishulam.form: Bend the thumb and little finger in and keep the index, middle and ring fingers straight, like the three prongs of a trident.
